summary.text: Polarity is a separation of electric charge in a molecule or chemical group, giving it a negatively charged end and a positively charged end.
It comes from electronegativity, the pull an atom exerts on its electrons, so shared electrons are drawn closer to the atom with the higher electronegativity.
Polarity underlies surface tension, solubility, and melting and boiling points, yet bond dipoles can cancel out in a symmetrical molecule.

facts.label: Br₂ dipole moment
facts.value: Zero, because the molecule is symmetrical

items.prompt: Two atoms are bonded, but one is far greedier for electrons than the other. Where do the shared electrons end up?

options.label: Spread evenly, midway between the two nuclei
Pushed away from both atoms into the surrounding space
Drawn closer to the atom with the higher electronegativity
Held by the atom with the lower electronegativity

items.explain: Electrons are drawn closer to the atom with higher electronegativity, so the sharing is unequal.

items.prompt: A molecule has bonds between unequal atoms, but as a whole it shows no separation of charge. What is the likely reason?

options.label: Its bond dipoles cancel each other out because of its symmetry
Unequal atoms always share electrons perfectly equally
Its bonds are ionic, which cannot create charge separation
The electrons in it have no charge

items.explain: Molecules with polar bonds have no molecular polarity if the bond dipoles cancel each other out by symmetry.

items.prompt: Two liquids have similar molar masses, but only one has molecules with charged ends. Which has the higher boiling point?

options.label: The one without charged ends, because its molecules are freer to leave
Neither, since similar masses always boil at the same temperature
The one with charged ends, because its atoms bond more strongly inside each molecule
The one with charged ends, because its molecules attract each other more

items.explain: Polar molecules interact through dipole-dipole intermolecular forces and hydrogen bonds, and polarity underlies melting and boiling points.

items.prompt: The electronegativity difference between two bonded atoms grows so large that one atom actually takes an electron from the other. What is the bond better called?

options.label: A nonpolar covalent bond
An ionic bond
A slightly polar covalent bond
A hydrogen bond

items.explain: A completely polar bond is more correctly called an ionic bond, where one atom actually takes an electron from the other.

items.prompt: Two bonds separate the same amount of charge, but in one the charges sit further apart. Which has the larger bond dipole moment?

options.label: The one with the smaller distance between charges
They are equal, since the amount of charge is the same
Neither, because distance does not matter for dipoles
The one with the larger distance between charges

items.explain: The bond dipole moment is calculated by multiplying the amount of charge separated by the distance between the charges.

items.prompt: Compare a molecule of two identical bromine atoms with a gas-phase potassium bromide pair. Which has the bigger dipole moment, and why?

options.label: Potassium bromide, because it is highly ionic
Bromine, because identical atoms pull hardest
Both are equal, because both contain bromine
Bromine, because symmetry makes dipoles add up

items.explain: Symmetrical Br₂ has zero dipole moment, while highly ionic gas-phase KBr has a dipole moment of 10.41 D.
